category.label: Calcium
category.comparisonNote: Costs use explicitly labelled elemental calcium per verified serving. Carbonate, citrate, citrate-malate and other salt masses are stored separately and never substituted for the mineral. Compare added nutrients separately and retain unknown amounts as unknown.

guide.title: Calcium: food intake, elemental amounts and bone health
guide.summary: Calcium is essential for bones and cell signalling. A useful supplement fills an assessed dietary gap; a large salt weight or a bone-health promise cannot establish that gap.
guide.evidence: Calcium supports normal mineralization and is part of care for selected bone and mineral disorders. Meeting requirements and treating osteoporosis are different tasks: calcium alone does not replace fracture-risk assessment or prescribed treatment.
guide.limitations: Studies of blanket supplementation in community-dwelling older adults have not consistently reduced fractures. Those findings do not mean that correcting low intake or a diagnosed mineral disorder is unnecessary; the population, vitamin D status and outcome matter.
guide.catalogReading: Compare explicitly labelled elemental calcium per label serving and its calculated cost. Calcium carbonate, citrate and citrate-malate name ingredients; their whole compound masses are not the calcium amount. Keep vitamin D, vitamin K2, magnesium and other co-ingredients separate.
guide.safety: Review kidney disease, previous stones, high blood calcium and medicines before supplementing. Excess can cause harm; constipation and bloating can limit tolerability. Calcium can reduce absorption of levothyroxine and some antibiotics or HIV medicines, so follow the medicine-specific spacing instructions with a pharmacist.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: The intestine absorbs calcium ions from food and dissolved supplement compounds through active and passive routes; active transport depends on vitamin D.
Most body calcium is held in bones and teeth. A small circulating pool supports muscle contraction, nerve signalling and other cellular functions.
Hormones coordinate intestinal absorption, kidney handling and bone turnover to maintain circulating calcium. A normal blood result does not prove that dietary intake has been adequate.
guide.treatment: Clinician-directed calcium is used in disorders such as hypocalcemia, calcium-deficiency rickets or osteomalacia and as nutritional support in osteoporosis care. Causes and vitamin D status must be assessed; an oral retail tablet is not a universal treatment for bone pain, cramps or an acute low-calcium episode.
guide.whoMayBenefit: People with persistently inadequate food intake, selected malabsorption problems, or a bone/mineral condition with an assessed need. Dairy avoidance can create a gap, but fortified foods and calcium-set tofu can help meet requirements without a tablet.
guide.routineUse: No group should automatically buy calcium merely because it trains, reaches a birthday or has a symptom. Estimate food intake and consider the relevant life stage before deciding whether any supplemental amount is needed.

whoCanConsider: Adults with a measured dietary shortfall that suitable foods cannot readily fill.
People with a diagnosed bone or mineral disorder whose clinician has specified calcium within a wider care plan.
whoShouldReview: Kidney impairment, kidney stones, high calcium levels or parathyroid disease need individual assessment.
People taking levothyroxine, certain antibiotics, dolutegravir or lithium should review timing and safety.

value.targetedUse: Filling a verified dietary gap or supporting an assessed bone/mineral care plan.
value.reason: The need for adequate calcium is established; the value of an extra tablet depends on intake, health context and the elemental amount actually provided.
worthWhen: Food intake has been assessed and a practical calcium gap remains.
The elemental amount, serving size, tolerability, medicine timing and total daily intake have been checked.
skipWhen: Adequate intake is already achieved without a supplement.
The purchase rests on a larger salt weight, a premium ingredient name or a guarantee of fracture prevention.
value.scope: Editorial priority for meeting calcium needs; not a score for treating osteoporosis, preventing every fracture or choosing a particular brand.

dos.title: Read elemental calcium per serving
dos.detail: Use the declared elemental milligrams and the number of tablets in the label serving. A compound quantity is a different measurement.

dos.title: Choose a form for the actual constraint
dos.detail: Carbonate is generally taken with food; citrate is less dependent on stomach acid. Consider tolerability and cost rather than assuming the most expensive salt is best.

dos.title: Count calcium from the whole day
dos.detail: Include food, fortified drinks, multivitamins, mineral stacks and calcium-containing antacids before choosing a gap-filling amount.

donts.title: Do not treat a daily target as a supplement dose
donts.detail: A 1,000 mg total-intake reference does not mean adding a 1,000 mg tablet to an already calcium-rich diet.

donts.title: Do not replace a clinical bone-health plan
donts.detail: A supplement does not substitute for assessment of fractures, osteoporosis, malabsorption or an abnormal blood calcium result.

donts.title: Do not cut out food calcium after a stone without advice
donts.detail: Stone prevention depends on the stone type and urine findings. Adequate food calcium can reduce intestinal oxalate absorption; supplements need separate review.

notes: The ICMR-NIN 2020 summary published by FSSAI lists 1,000 mg/day calcium for adult men and women across sedentary, moderate and heavy-work categories. This is an Indian total-intake reference, not a supplemental dose.
No dose multiplier is assigned to two, three or five sessions a week, bodybuilding experience, CrossFit, HYROX or powerlifting.
Pregnancy, lactation, adolescents and treatment of mineral disorders need their own assessment. Adult references should not be applied to children.
Higher labelling percentages, larger compound weights and the upper limit do not establish a need for more calcium.

medicalGuide.summary: Calcium has established nutritional and selected clinical uses, while evidence for routine preventive tablets depends on the population. Clinical replacement is distinct from self-treating symptoms.

conditions.findings: Calcium replacement can be part of treatment after identifying the cause; rickets, osteomalacia and hypoparathyroidism may require specific management. Acute symptomatic hypocalcemia is not a retail self-care problem.
conditions.limits: Vitamin D, magnesium, kidney function and the underlying diagnosis can change the regimen.

conditions.findings: Adequate calcium and vitamin D support a broader osteoporosis plan. A tablet alone does not reverse every cause of bone fragility or replace indicated medicines, exercise and fall-risk management.
conditions.limits: An adequate total intake is supportive care, not a guarantee of fracture prevention.

conditions.condition: Routine fracture prevention in community-dwelling older adults
conditions.findings: A systematic review of randomized trials did not find reduced fracture incidence from routine calcium, vitamin D or their combination in community-dwelling adults older than 50. This population is distinct from selected deficient patients or institutional care.
conditions.limits: Do not extrapolate this result to withholding needed replacement or stopping an existing treatment plan.

conditions.findings: Appropriate food calcium may help bind oxalate in the gut. Stone history is a reason to individualize supplements, not to eliminate calcium-rich foods automatically.
conditions.limits: Stone type, urine results and kidney function determine the plan.

pathway.title: From intestinal calcium to a regulated mineral pool
pathway.summary: Calcium is a mineral ion, not a protein or an energy source. Its movement between intestine, blood, kidney and bone is regulated.

steps.label: Food and compounds release calcium
steps.detail: Digestion and dissolution make calcium available for intestinal absorption. Vitamin D supports active uptake.

steps.label: A small blood pool supplies tissues
steps.detail: Circulating calcium supports signalling, nerve activity and muscle contraction; blood levels are tightly controlled.

steps.label: Bone stores calcium in mineral
steps.detail: Bone deposition and resorption exchange calcium with the circulating pool as part of lifelong remodelling.

steps.label: Kidneys and hormones adjust balance
steps.detail: Renal handling and hormonal feedback help maintain calcium balance alongside intestinal absorption and bone turnover.

pathway.caveat: A normal physiological role does not prove that an extra tablet improves strength or prevents a fracture. Blood calcium is not a simple dietary-intake score.
